title: I kept working on my historical city builder game - Pixel Metropolis
author: Odd_Revolution7522
selftext:
Hello again, r/aigamedev!

Almost a month ago, I posted my game here for the first time and got a lot of cool comments and reactions.



To be frank, I didn’t make as much progress on the actual game as I’d hoped. I was focused on creating the Steam page, registering for Steam Next Fest, preparing demo builds and marketing assets, doing outreach, etc....all the mandatory parts of creating a “serious” game that AI can’t quite automate 100% yet, haha.



Anyway, I’m back at it, and this time I’ve got a functioning early Antiquity gameplay loop up to around 1,500 population. The era is planned to go all the way to 15,000, so it’s a big one. It’s been pretty cool watching my settlement become progressively Romanized and being able to spin up asset variations quickly.



Here’s a timelapse I find pretty: a settlement growing from 0 to 1,000 population, from Prehistory to early Antiquity.



The demo build “only” covers the Paleolithic, Neolithic, and Metal Age, but it’s already a meaty one, with a median playtime of 39 minutes and an average of 85 minutes.



I can’t wait to really convey the awe and scale of Antiquity in the game. I feel like AI is at its strongest when it comes to creating asset variety. Even my lowly early Antiquity peasants have three different building types, with four variations each. That’s a volume of asset variety that would previously have been completely impossible for me to produce.

comments.author: Baraga91
comments.body:
I loved playing games like this when I was a kid!

What's the core game loop about? Sim Cit or Anno?

And when you say "Metal Age", I assume you mean iron age and not the Rolling Stones, right? 😛

replies.author: Odd_Revolution7522
replies.body:
It’s more Sim City 4 than Anno yes ! Actually light on logistics simulation and more about urbanism and influencing the city.

Haha for Metal Age I lumped together Bronze and Iron Age (don’t want to end up with 15 eras) so it’s basically post Neolithic and pre-Roman, loosely Celtic era.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body: What would be wrong with 15 eras? 😁

replies.author: Odd_Revolution7522
replies.body: Even with AI, scope creep shall be avoided ;)

comments.author: Afterlight_Games
comments.body:
Yooo the settlement progression looks really cool! The amount of building variety is impressive too.

I just got my own game onto Steam and I feel you on how much time all the non development stuff eats up lol. Between the store page, trailer, promotional assets, and marketing, it's almost like having a second project on top of the game itself

How are you handling consistency between all the Ai generated building variations? That's something I've been working on with my own assets

replies.author: Odd_Revolution7522
replies.body:
Thanks !  
I explained my workflow in my latest post on the sub, basically a good step by step process and initial concept art generation with a game screenshot as the basis with isometric grid on.

comments.author: Necessary-Soft910
comments.body:
Beautiful! Which harness did you use?

Did you generate the assets by your own ?

replies.author: Odd_Revolution7522
replies.body: It's all made inside Codex, assets are generated with the imagegen tool.

replies.author: Necessary-Soft910
replies.body:
Great! I’m making a poc for a pixelart 2d project but facing some issues .. currently I’m manually approving asset by asset otherwise doing it in batch mode are giving me headaches such as low fidelity quality .

How are you dealing with it ? And are u using Astra or Sol ?

replies.author: Odd_Revolution7522
replies.body:
I’m using Sol but yes I do it step by step :  
\- concept generation   
\- approved SW view  
\- approved NW view  
\- mirroring and atlas generation 

Batch generation drifts too much.

I think it is sane to remind ourselves that even that workflow takes less than one hour per asset instead of 2-3 days by hand.

Assets variations without changing geometry are lighting fast though.

replies.author: Necessary-Soft910
replies.body: Cool! thanks for the heads upand great work!
